Respondents For Petitioners : Dr. Shiv Kumar Shrivastava, Advocate For Respondents : Mr. Akash Shrivastava on behalf of Mr. R.N. Pusty, Advocate Hon'ble Shri Arvind Kumar Verma, Judge Order on Board 08/10/2024 1.

Claimant-appellant has filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 for enhancement and modification of the award, challenging the impugned award dated 26.03.2018 awarded by the 4th Additional Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, Raipur (C.G.) in Claim Case No.
463/2016, whereby the Tribunal allowed appliation filed under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 in part,
calculated total compensation of Rs. 9,57,425/- on account of death of the deceased Late Nand Kumar Baghel in this claim petition.
2. The case in nutshell is that on 02.11.2014 the deceased was going from his home to Raipur, his village on Hero motorcycle CD Deluxe bearing registration no. CG 04 KD 7190 and at about 11:00 am one Hyva truck bearing registration no. CG 15 AC 2467 was coming from the opposite side at a very high speed and crushes the deceased near overbridge at Vidhan Sabha, Saddu Raipur and run away with the said truck.

entities.text: 4th Additional Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, Raipur (C.G.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The deceased was taken to Balaji Hospital for medical treatment and on 09.11.2014 the deceased died in the hospital.

3. Appellants have filed an application under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 seeking total compensation of Rs. 74,87,726/- pleading therein that on the date of accident, the deceased was farmer and was earning Rs. 4,50,000/- annually.
4.

Respondent no. 1 has submitted his written statement in which he has denied all the contentions raised by the appellants in their claim petition stating that at the time of incident the vehicle was insured with Respondent No. 3/insurance company and the driver of the vehicle was having an effective and valid license, therefore if any liability arises out of the said accident then it should be burdened upon respondent no. 3/insurance company.
5. Respondent no. 3/insurance company submitted its written reply in which they have opposed the said facts of the appellant relating to the accident.

Insurance company submitted that at the time of incident, respondent no. 1/driver of the vehicle was not having an effective and valid driving license still he drove the vehicle, hence he clearly violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Respondent no. 3 is not liable to pay any compensation which arises out of the said accident.

Hence,
pleads to reject the application against him.

6. Upon appreciation of pleadings and evidence placed on record by respective parties, Tribunal held that the appellant sustained grievous injuries due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle/respondent no. 1.

Accordingly, Tribunal allowed application in part, awarded Rs. 9,57,425/- with interest @ 7.5% per annum, fastened liability upon Respondent no. 3 to pay the Smt. Krishna Baghel vs Vinod Kumar Yadav on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121488671/
2 amount of compensation.

sentences.text:
7. Learned Counsel appearing for the appellants submitted that the impugned award is illegal,
erroneous, unjustified and contrary to law.
He further contended that the learned claims Tribunal has wrongly assessed the monthly income of the appellant.

Amount awarded for medical treatment,
travelling and special diet are on lower side.
8. Learned counsel appearing for respondent no. 2 and 3 opposes the prayer made by the learned Counsel for the appellants/claimants.
Claims Tribunal after taking into consideration documents placed on record by the Claimants has awarded total amount of compensation of Rs. 9,57,425/-.

Hence, amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal to claimants cannot be said to be on lower side, rather it is just and proper and in the given facts and circumstances of the case and does not call for any interference.
9.
I have heard counsel for the parties at length, considered their rival submissions and perused the records with utmost circumspection.

10. As regards the income of the appellant, though the claimant have pleaded in the claim petition that the deceased was earning Rs. 4,50,000/- annually but no documentary evidence in support thereof has been adduced by the appellant to substantiate the said fact.
However, the Tribunal assessed the notional income of the claimant as Rs. 6,000/- per month, which in the considered opinion of this Court is neither on the higher side nor on the lower side.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that there is no need to recompute the compensation as regards the income of the deceased.
11. On perusal of record, this Court finds that the learned Tribunal has rightly assessed the notional income of the deceased as Rs. 6,000/- per month.
As he was married man left behind wife and one major son, therefore Tribunal has granted 1/3 rd deduction towards personal expenses.
Looking to the age of the deceased which was 54 years at the time of incident tribunal has applied an appropriate multiplier of 11 and rightly awarded future prospects @ 10%.

The Tribunal has rightly awarded Rs. 15,000/- for funeral expenses, Rs. 40,000/- towards spousal consortium, Rs. 15,000/-
for loss of estate.

However, the Tribunal has not granted any amount toward loss of parental consortium to the appellant no. 2 which in the opinion of this Court should be benefited under the head of loss of parental consortium.

12. In the light of judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matters of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs.
Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2009) 6 SCC 121 and Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs.

For the foregoing reasons, the appeal is allowed in part.

The amount of compensation of Rs.
9,57,425/- awarded by the tribunal is enhanced to Rs. 9,97,425/-.
Hence, after deducting the amount of Rs. 9,57,425/- the appellants are entitled for an additional amount of Rs. 40,000/-.
The insurance company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation as enhanced by this Court within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
The additional amount of compensation shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of claim application before the Tribunal, till its realization.
Rest of the conditions of impugned award shall remain intact.
14. As a result, appeal is allowed in part and the impugned award modified to the extent as indicated herein-above.

The deposit tribunal shall pass appropriate order with regard to apportionment,
investment and disbursement fo the enhanced amount of compensation.
15. The cross-objection filed by the Respondent No. 3 under Order 41 Rule 22 of CPC, 1908 read with Rule 242(3) of C.G. Motor Vehicles Rule, 1994 is hereby dismissed.
